If a second carrier number later appears, append it to the same case and say which units are still unresolved. Opening a new enquiry without cross-references can leave two people investigating the same parcel under different assumptions. When the issue is resolved, note whether the explanation was a split seller package, a separate intake record or an actual shortage. This matters if you later need a refund or replacement for a specific unit.

During international transit, a similar approach helps when the platform and carrier display different events. Quote both rather than treating one as inherently authoritative. For example, say that the platform lists dispatch on one date and the carrier still shows label creation as its latest public event. Ask which record establishes physical handover and whether a carrier enquiry is available yet. Include the tracking number privately and avoid guessing a delivery date from the gap.

As the parcel moves, one line per physical handoff is usually enough. You do not need to save a fresh screenshot every time you refresh an unchanged page. Save the events that change a decision, such as warehouse receipt, payment confirmation, carrier acceptance, a delivery exception or final receipt. This compact history will be easier to use than dozens of repeated screenshots if support later asks which handoff you are querying.

If you share the timeline with a family member waiting for the parcel, provide the international tracking link only after you have identified it. The domestic reference can send them looking for a delivery in the wrong country.

faq.q: Which marketplace links does FansBuy’s buying guide mention?
faq.a: The guide gives Taobao, 1688 and Weidian as examples for the link search. After opening the link, check the seller, selected option and quantity in the imported item.

faq.q: What if FansBuy keyword search returns the wrong version?
faq.a: Try the original seller URL. Compare the seller and exact option with your saved listing before adding it to the cart.

faq.q: Can I send a purchase request without automatic product import?
faq.a: The beginner guide describes a fill-and-buy option. Enter the source, specifications and quantity yourself, and ask about any essential detail the seller has not confirmed.

faq.q: Does paying for an item include international delivery?
faq.a: FansBuy describes paying for goods and China-side delivery first. Review and pay for the international parcel after warehouse arrival.

faq.q: Can I use FansBuy account balance at checkout?
faq.a: The guide describes a Use Balance option. Check the deduction and any remaining amount on the actual payment screen.

faq.q: Where do I request additional order services?
faq.a: The beginner guide points to the value-added services action in My orders and to customer service for special requests. Confirm availability and price for the item.

faq.q: Where do processed warehouse items appear?
faq.a: Look in the Packing Centre under your personal account. Match each record to the original order before selecting it for shipment.

faq.q: What does FansBuy do when goods reach its warehouse?
faq.a: Its buying guide describes an intake check, weighing and photos. Read the evidence for the item you ordered before deciding to ship.

faq.q: Can a QC photo show whether a jacket fits?
faq.a: A photo can show a size label or visible measurements. Compare matching measurements with a garment that fits you, and ask for a specific view if an essential measurement is missing.

faq.q: How much free storage does FansBuy advertise?
faq.a: The official site advertises 90 days. Check your item’s dates and any account-specific notices before waiting for other orders.

faq.q: Can I send some stored products now and wait for others?
faq.a: The guide lets you select products in the Packing Centre for parcel submission. Confirm which item references you have selected before authorising the parcel.

faq.q: What is a FansBuy rehearsal package?
faq.a: The guide describes paid packing and measurement before you choose the logistics method and pay final shipping. Check the service charge and available packing instructions on your parcel.

faq.q: Do I need a parcel’s weight or its dimensions for an estimate?
faq.a: Prepare gross weight and outside dimensions, destination and contents. Read the billing and eligibility rules of the routes shown for that parcel.

faq.q: Does smaller packaging always reduce shipping cost?
faq.a: It depends on the route. A minimum, gross-weight charge or rounding rule may leave the price unchanged even when the box occupies less space.

faq.q: What happens if FansBuy's freight estimate is too high?
faq.a: The official guide says the excess is credited to the account balance. Match the parcel’s final statement to the corresponding balance entry.

faq.q: What happens if the shipping deposit is too low?
faq.a: FansBuy describes requesting the remaining amount before shipment. Check the parcel notice and balance history before paying again.

faq.q: Can a shipping adjustment use my account balance automatically?
faq.a: The beginner guide describes an optional pre-authorised amount that can be deducted when sufficient balance is available. Check the current setting and transaction record.

faq.q: Where do I check insurance conditions?
faq.a: Use the current parcel offer and the Insurance and Compensation material in FansBuy’s Help Center. Verify covered events and the insured value for your own shipment.

faq.q: How do I track a dispatched FansBuy parcel?
faq.a: Use Track shipping for the international parcel. Keep its parcel reference separate from seller-to-warehouse tracking numbers.

faq.q: What does a domestic tracking status of delivered mean?
faq.a: Check the destination. A China-side delivery scan can concern the FansBuy warehouse, with inspection and international shipment still to follow.

faq.q: What should I send support about a parcel cost difference?
faq.a: Provide the parcel reference, currency, deposit, final amount, optional charges and the entry you cannot reconcile. Share only the parts of receipts needed to explain the issue.
